newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P affirms Sirius claims paying ability at A+.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Sirius claims paying ability at A+.

text.p: Standard & Poor's on Friday affirmed its claims paying ability rating for Sweden's Sirius International Insurance Corp at A+.
Sirius is part of international engineering group Asea Brown Boveri (ABB).
S&P said the rating affirmation was based on the company's conservative, profit-driven philosophies, excellent capitalisation, a good Nordic business position and a strong earnings profile.

But it said in a statement that these strengths were partly offset by its limited franchise outside the Nordic region, its dependence on premium volume in order to maintain capital levels and S&P's view that the group was not an intergral part of ABB.
S&P expected the management profit requirement to remain firm and not be relaxed in the pursuit of new business growth.

It also said it expected the group's capitalisation to remain excellent and that moderate growth of the traditional reinsurance business would be achieved. It said that ABB-related business growth would be more significant.
S&P said the combined ratio was expected to weaken slightly in line with expansion plans and the competitive environment but S&P said it regarded the 104 percent ceiling set as realistic.
S&P said that ROR would fall slightly although investment earnings from the capital base would provide stability at the bottom line.
